# e-JCPP (Electronic Journal of Cardiovascular Prevention and Pharmacotherapy)

> > An open-access peer-reviewed medical journal dedicated to advancing knowledge in cardiovascular prevention, pharmacotherapy, and disease management.

e-JCPP is a leading open-access journal published by Korea University that publishes original research, reviews, and clinical insights on cardiovascular disease prevention and pharmacological interventions. The journal serves the global cardiovascular medicine community with rigorous peer review and freely accessible content.

## Key Topics

- Cardiovascular diseases
- Hypertension
- Pharmacotherapy
- Cardiovascular prevention
- Peer review
- Open access
- Diabetes mellitus
- Sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibitors
- Research ethics
- Publication ethics
- Medical journal
- Stroke
- Lipoprotein(a)
- Korea University
- KSCP/KSCVP

## Journal Content & Articles

- [Current Issue](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/current.php): Current issue of e-JCPP with latest cardiovascular prevention and pharmacotherapy articles.
- [Article Archive](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/archive.php): Journal article archive and repository for published research.
- [Ahead-of-Print Articles](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/print.php): Ahead-of-print articles for e-JCPP cardiovascular research.
- [Articles by Category](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/category.php): Articles categorized by topic: cardiovascular diseases, hypertension, diabetes mellitus.
- [Most-Read Articles](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/mostread.php): Most-viewed articles in Cardiovascular Prevention and Pharmacotherapy journal.
- [Most-Downloaded Articles](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/mostdownload.php): Most-downloaded articles on sodium-glucose transporter 2 inhibitors and cardiovascular diseases.
- [Most-Cited Articles](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/mostcited.php): Most-cited research articles in Cardiovascular Prevention and Pharmacotherapy.
- [Funded Research](https://e-jcpp.org/articles/funded.php): Funded research articles on hypertension, cardiovascular diseases, and coronary artery disease.
